newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-NORWAY'S MARKEN FASTEST IN FINAL RUN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-NORWAY'S MARKEN FASTEST IN FINAL RUN.

text.p: -Ingeborg Helen Marken of Norway raced through a mounting snowstorm on Thursday to record the fastest time in the second and final training run for a Friday World Cup downhill.

Marken's time, 1:50.16, was dramatically faster than that of runnerup Katja Seizinger of Germany, timed in 1:51.08. Alexandra Meissnitzer of Austria was third in 1:51.45, followed by Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden in 1:51.58.

All of the fastest times came from racers who chose later start positions on a course peppered by snow from a major Pacific storm pushing into the Colorado Rockies. Apparently, the course became faster as subsequent starters packed the track.

"Visibility wasn't as bad as one would expect," said Hilary Lindh of the United States, who must carry the burden for her team after the Wednesday season-ending injury to Picabo Street, the defending World Cup downhill champion. Street tore the anterior cruciate ligament in her left knee in a training crash.
Friday's weather forecast is not promising: an accumulation of up to a foot of snow, cold and possibly high winds.
